title: Promotion/soak qualification evidence must be structurally verifiable, reset-traceable, and gate-drift-detectable
requirement: Where a Clank qualifies a collector or source for production via soak/natural-cycle evidence, that evidence MUST be structurally verifiable from the Clank's own stored data, not merely asserted in documentation or an operator's memory. Specifically: (1) wherever the distinction between natural/scheduled, manual, deploy-verification, and recovery/diagnostic execution affects qualification, the execution path itself MUST record enough provenance to make that distinction after the fact; (2) a material code, configuration, or source change that invalidates prior qualification evidence MUST start or reset the qualification window, with the reset decision recorded (what changed, and why it was judged material); (3) an operational incident, host migration, or manual recovery action MUST NOT itself reset accumulated qualification evidence, and MUST NOT be silently counted as ordinary natural-cycle evidence unless the Clank's own policy explicitly permits that class of evidence; (4) where more than one gate governs promotion/production eligibility, divergence between those gates MUST be detectable, and MUST fail closed (treated as not-yet-eligible) rather than silently promoting through whichever gate was updated.
trigger: Applies to any Clank with a soak/promotion lifecycle for collectors or sources, where qualification evidence is used to justify a production decision. A Clank with no promotion lifecycle (every source is production-eligible immediately, with nothing to qualify) is out of scope by trigger. Does not require any specific cycle count, duration, or maturity state machine — those remain per-Clank policy parameters. Does not require a single-gate architecture — multiple gates are permitted provided divergence between them is detectable and fails closed.
rationale: Near-universal independent convergence on the material-change-resets-the-clock principle across four Clanks, in every case currently recorded only as human/narrative judgment rather than code-enforced. The clearest, most severe incident evidence is a dual-gate promotion near-miss: two independently-maintained gates had to both agree before a source's data was trusted as production-scope; only one was updated during a real promotion, and the gap was caught only same-day, averting roughly 18 false alerts that would otherwise have fired against devices the Clank had never legitimately recorded. semiconductor-intelligence's scheduler-routing design proves that structurally verifiable trigger provenance is achievable, not merely aspirational, while roughly half the surveyed fleet has no verifiable trigger field at all — one Clank's promotion evidence for a natural-cadence proof exists only as a YAML comment, unverifiable from the database itself. clank-architecture Fleet Law 8 (ACTIVE, CI-enforced) already names promotion-gate integrity as governance, with three separate historical violators on record. A separate architectural draft (clank-architecture ADR-0006, not yet ACTIVE) independently states that a soak/QC clock must not be reset by an incident, with affected evidence instead reporting as not-yet-measurable rather than reset to zero or silently discarded — this standard adopts that same incident-does-not-reset principle as part of its own acceptance criteria, citing ADR-0006 as its source rather than restating its full text.
forbidden: Treating a manually-invoked or deploy-verification run as equivalent to natural-cadence qualification evidence with no recorded, verifiable distinction between them
Silently discarding, merging, or resetting accumulated qualification evidence in response to an operational incident, host migration, or manual recovery action
Resetting a qualification window for a material change without recording that a reset occurred and why
Promoting a source to production through one gate while a second, independently-maintained gate that should also have been updated silently remains in its prior state
Treating passing test/CI success, or a clean build, as self-authorizing promotion beyond whatever the Clank's own qualification evidence actually demonstrates
acceptance: Wherever qualification depends on the natural-vs-manual-vs-deploy-vs-recovery distinction, that provenance is recoverable from the execution path's own recorded data, not solely from operator memory or free-text documentation
A qualification-window reset triggered by a material change is accompanied by a recorded build/change identity and a stated reason

Qualification evidence accumulated before an operational incident, host migration, or manual recovery action remains intact afterward, or is explicitly marked not-yet-measurable for the affected scope — it is not silently zeroed or discarded

An operator intervention performed during a qualification window is distinguishable from a natural qualification cycle in the Clank's own records; interventions are never required to be forbidden, only distinguishable and non-qualifying unless policy explicitly says otherwise

Where multiple promotion/eligibility gates exist, an automated or structural check exists that can detect the gates disagreeing, and the disagreement resolves to not-yet-eligible rather than to promoted

evidence.summary: Two independent, uncross-checked promotion/scope gates; only one was updated during a real promotion, and a baseline-completion tracker marked the source qualified despite 18 real candidates being silently dropped by the other gate — caught same-day, averting the false alerts the next scheduled run would otherwise have produced.

No source reaches production scheduling without soak evidence, an explicit promotion record, and rollback state; three separate historical violators (tablet, smartwatch, oem-radar) are named on record.
Proves structurally-verifiable trigger provenance is achievable: the scheduled path is required to route through the scheduler so a direct invocation cannot masquerade as a natural trigger.

One Clank's natural-cadence promotion proof exists only as a YAML comment, unverifiable from the database; a second's trigger field is self-asserted by a CLI flag never cross-checked against the actual scheduler.
States a QC/soak clock must not be reset by an operational incident; affected gates instead report as unmeasurable/not-yet-mature rather than reset to zero.

An operator manually aborted a soak campaign mid-run to relocate hosts; handled correctly by excluding the partial cycles from later promotion-counting evidence, demonstrating interventions can be distinguishable without being forbidden.

notes: Pass 1 draft (docs/operations/pass1/dossier-ops-c-promotion-soak-evidence-integrity.md), from Pass 0B adjudication candidate OPS-C (docs/operations/pass0/candidates/ops-c-promotion-soak-evidence-integrity.md), merging Pass 0A clusters natural-cycle-vs-manual-trigger-provenance-gap, soak-clock-reset-semantics-and-material-change-judgment, dual-gate-promotion-authority-drift, and safe-manual-intervention-during-soak (docs/operations/pass0/clusters/). Deliberately does not standardize cycle counts, soak duration, or a single maturity state machine — these remain per-Clank policy parameters, per Pass 0B's explicit instruction. Does not mandate a single-gate promotion architecture — tablet-clank's cascade-demotion-through-both-gates design and feature-phone-clank's single-gate design are both cited as conforming, structurally different solutions to the same drift-detectability requirement. NARROW COMPLEMENT to clank-architecture Fleet Law 8 (ACTIVE): Law 8 owns promotion-gate authority itself and is not restated; this standard ratifies the evidence-verifiability, reset-traceability, and drift-detectability slice Law 8 leaves open. References, does not restate or incorporate by reference, clank-architecture ADR-0006's incident-does-not-reset principle (PROPOSED at drafting time, not ACTIVE). Standards Clank defines the semantic invariant; clank-architecture's Fleet Laws and ADRs remain separate authority unless a later governance decision migrates or supersedes them — this standard does not claim to replace clank-architecture, and clank-architecture itself was not modified by this drafting pass. PROPOSED — awaiting Pass 2 adversarial review and eventual operator ratification; not yet ratified, not self-ratified.
